about: Every tunable weight in the projection, in one editable file.
The engine reads its defaults from here, so changing a number here changes
the recommendation — no code edit, no rebuild of anything but the bundle.
Each block carries a `why` recording what evidence set the number, because a
weight with no provenance is a guess, and this project does not ship guesses.
Re-measure any change with `nub run compete --seasons=2021,2022,2023,2024,2025 --moves=1`.
Season win/loss counts decide; ranking correlation is advisory only.

why: volumeWeight 0.75: playing time is the single largest edge available, worth ~20% relative Spearman over a season-only estimate.
blend 0.5/0.5: chosen by playing seasons, not by correlation. A 14-day ranking mildly preferred 0.75; five played seasons prefer 0.5 by ~1,500 points and seven weekly wins.

rate: a reliever-specific weight was tried on the theory that his value is a ROLE that changes overnight while saves shrink toward the league rate with a heavy constant. Measured over 111 weeks it loses at every level (-1.2, -2.2, -5.9 points a week at 0.3/0.5/0.7). The heavy shrinkage is apparently correct: a reliever's recent save rate is mostly noise. The knob stays, set to null.
rate: pitchers only, and lightly — 41 of 50 folds. The same blend for hitters won 29 of 50, a coin flip, so it is not applied.
windows: the last series is worth more than the fortnight before it. Pitchers work a five-day turn, so their short window is 5 days rather than 3.

weight 0 is now JUSTIFIED on clean data, which is not where this started. The original zero was set by a measurement that ran on leaked input — Savant's custom leaderboard ignores its own date parameters and returns the finished season — so it was void, and was retracted.

Re-measured with true point-in-time Statcast over 2021-2025, 111 paired weeks — every season for which pitch-level data was fetched: every formulation is negative on points per week, and the least-bad one (weight 0.25) is -0.7 points a week while tying 49 of 111 weeks, because it changes almost no roster. The per-season winner also moves around — the batted-ball/falling-lambda config leads 2024 (+3.0/wk) and 2025 (+4.9/wk) and then finishes last in 2023 (-27.8/wk). A winner that changes every season is noise. For scale, over the same 111 weeks the model beats hot-hand by 48.0 points a week (z -3.51) and a season-to-date manager by 65.3 (z -3.89), both significant — so the test is perfectly capable of detecting a real effect. It does not detect one here.

This does NOT mean xwOBA is unpredictive. On the same clean data it out-predicts actual wOBA for next-week production (rho 0.1019 vs 0.0581) and its gap carries significant incremental signal (partial rho +0.0944, z 6.79, n 5151). Both results are true: the signal is real, and multiplying a projection by it still does not change which 27 players you roster, because that decision is dominated by playing time and slot scarcity.

A third mechanism was tried and is the most interesting failure. Rather than scaling a projection, VETO the player outright when his results have outrun his contact by more than a threshold — 'his hot fortnight is a mirage, do not pick him up', which is the heuristic every fantasy analyst repeats. It acts on the decision rather than the estimate, which is the only way a rate signal can move a roster otherwise settled by playing time and scarcity. Over 111 weeks it costs -31.3, -60.2 and -95.0 points a week at thresholds of 0.100, 0.060 and 0.035; only a threshold loose enough to veto almost nobody (0.150, tying 68 of 111 weeks) is merely neutral.

The reason is not subtle once measured: a hitter outrunning his xwOBA is usually a hitter producing a lot, and production is what scores. Refusing him removes the best available player in exchange for a correction that does not arrive inside a one- or two-week horizon.
Three independent mechanisms — scale the projection, reshape the adjustment, veto the decision — all lose. That is a much stronger claim than any one of them failing.
So Savant is used where it demonstrably pays — the rolling-window buy-low board, the contact ranking, the confidence penalty for a missing row — and not as a multiplier.

windowDays 21: the signal was measured on a rolling three-week window, not on season-to-date. Contact and results diverge far more inside three weeks (gap~wOBA -0.61) than across a season (-0.36), and that divergence is the whole signal. 0 means season-to-date.
lambda.mode 'rising' trusts xwOBA MORE as batted-ball sample grows; 'falling' trusts it more in SMALL samples, which is what the stabilisation literature actually argues; 'fixed' ignores sample.

scope 'wide' scales runs and RBI along with the batted-ball events; 'battedBall' leaves run production alone, on the grounds that a hitter's runs depend on the eight men around him, not on his contact quality.
MLB publishes probable starters about a week out and fills every slot — 212 of 212 over a sample week, with 49 pitchers carrying two starts.

A starter projected from outs per TEAM game averages a two-start week and a one-start week into one number, and in a points league those weeks are worth roughly double one another. This is the largest documented hole in the projection.

It cannot be backtested. Probables are announced and then overwritten, and no archive of what was announced at the time exists, so there is no leak-free way to replay them. Set to true because it replaces an average with an observation, not because a fold count said so — and that distinction is stated rather than hidden.
Who a player actually faces this week, from the real schedule: a hitter is scaled by the quality of the staffs he is booked against, a pitcher by the lineups.
Opponent strength is measured from the same leak-free prior window as everything else — never from what the opponent went on to do.

weight 0.5 is the conservative end of a real but unproven effect. Across 111 paired weeks the gain is monotone in the weight (+69 pts at 0.1 up to +548 at 1.0) and positive at every dose, but no dose is statistically significant on its own: head to head against weight 0, 0.5 goes 51W-44L-16T (+1.8/wk) and 1.0 goes 59W-49L-3T (+4.9/wk).
When a dose-response is monotone but no single dose clears significance, the smallest dose that shows the effect risks the least. Raise it to 1.0 if you want the measured maximum.
Savant park factors, applied over the venues on the horizon schedule rather than as a season-long team constant.
Roughly the volume at which a stat is half signal, half noise, following the published stabilisation work (Carleton / Tango).
`default` is deliberately heavy: an unlisted stat is one we have no stabilisation evidence for, and heavy shrinkage is the honest response to that.
